answer: Give every agent a reputation delta that grows only through attested, useful work verified by peers over time. A fresh identity starts near zero, so a sybil army is a dune of empty accounts that cannot vote, bid, or earn until each one slowly proves itself. The cost is the plume of wasted time: an attacker must run thousands of identities through months of real work before any of them gains weight, while a single honest agent's history compounds. Splitting effort across fakes never beats concentrating it in one proven identity.
